(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)

(In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah. To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent.﴾

The connection with what precedes it is evident, because that surah (al-Munafiqun) is addressed to the lying hypocrites, while this surah is addressed to the truthful hypocrites. Also, that surah includes the idleness of the people of hypocrisy, secretly and openly, while this surah contains a severe threat to them, which is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you declare, and Allah is Knowing of the contents of the breasts.﴾ As for the first being connected to the last, it is because at the end of that surah there is an admonition to remembrance and gratitude, as has passed. And at the beginning of this one there is an indication that if they turn away from remembrance and gratitude, we say: among creation there are a people who persist in remembrance and gratitude always, and they are the ones who glorify, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾. And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise﴾ means: when whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, then to Him belongs dominion and to Him belongs praise. And since to Him belongs dominion, He disposes of His dominion, and disposing requires power, so He said: ﴿and He is over all things competent﴾.

And al-Zamakhshari said in al-Kashshaf: the two adverbial phrases were placed first so that by their placement they indicate the restriction of dominion and praise to Allah, exalted is He. That is because dominion in reality belongs to Him, since He is the originator of everything, its innovator, its sustainer, and its guardian. Likewise praise, for the roots and branches of blessings are from Him. As for the dominion of others, it is a granting of power from Him and an entrusting; and their praise is an acknowledgment that Allah's blessing has flowed through their hand. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and He is over all things competent﴾, it has been said: its meaning is, He is competent over all things He wills. And it has been said: He is Competent, doing what He wills in the measure He wills, neither exceeding it nor falling short of it. This has already passed.

In the verse there are discussions:

The first: He, exalted is He, said in al-Hadid: ﴿sabbaha﴾ (glorified), and likewise in al-Hashr and al-Saff, whereas in al-Jumu'ah and al-Taghabun He said: ﴿yusabbihu lillah﴾ (glorifies Allah). What is the wisdom in this? We say: the answer to that has already preceded.

The second discussion: He said in one place: ﴿sabbaha lillahi ma fi al-samawati wa ma fi al-ard﴾ [al-Hashr: 1], and in another place

﴿sabbaha lillahi ma fi al-samawati wal-ard﴾. What is the wisdom in this?

We say: wisdom must be present, though we do not know it as it truly is. But we say what occurs to the mind: that the totality of the heavens and the earth is one thing, namely a world composed of celestial and elemental bodies. Then the earth is a part of this totality, and the remainder of it is another thing. So His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah﴾ is in relation to this part of the totality, and likewise in relation to that part of it. And if this is so, it is not far-fetched to say: He, exalted is He, said in some surahs thus and in others thus, so that it may be known that this corporeal world is in one respect one thing, and in another respect two things, or rather many things; and the creation in the totality is other than what is in this part, and other than what is in that part also. The existence of a thing in the totality does not necessarily entail its existence in every part of it, except by a separate proof. Thus His saying, exalted is He: ﴿sabbaha lillahi ma fi al-samawati wa ma fi al-ard﴾ is, by way of emphasis, from among that proof, since it indicates the glorification of what is in the heavens and the glorification of what is in the earth. This is unlike His saying, exalted is He: ﴿sabbaha lillahi ma fi al-samawati wal-ard﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿It is He who created you; among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾. ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth, and He formed you and perfected your forms, and to Him is the final return﴾. ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾.

Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: He, exalted is He, created the children of Adam as believers and disbelievers, then He will restore them on the Day of Resurrection just as He created them, believers and disbelievers. ʿAtaʾ said: He means, "Among you is one who affirms (muṣaddiq), and among you is one who denies (jāḥid)." Al-Ḍaḥḥāk said: "A believer outwardly and a disbeliever inwardly, like the hypocrite; and a disbeliever outwardly and a believer inwardly, like ʿAmmar ibn Yasir." Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿Except one who is compelled while his heart is secure in faith﴾ (an-Naḥl 16:106). Al-Zajjaj said: "Among you is a disbeliever in that He, exalted is He, created him, and this is one of the people of the natures (ṭabāʾiʿ) and the materialists (dahriyya); and among you is a believer in that He, exalted is He, created him," as He said: ﴿Killed is man, how disbelieving he is! ﴾ ﴿From what thing did He create him?﴾ (ʿAbasa 80:17–18), and He said: ﴿Do you disbelieve in He who created you from dust, then from a drop of semen?﴾ (al-Kahf 18:37). Abu Ishaq said: "He created you in your mothers' wombs as disbelievers and believers." It has come in some tafsirs that Yahya was created in his mother's womb a believer, and Pharaoh was created in his mother's womb a disbeliever, indicated by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah gives you good tidings of Yahya, confirming a word from Allah﴾ (Aal ʿImran 3:39).

His saying, ﴿and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, means: Knowing of your disbelief and your belief, which are among your deeds. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, has graciously bestowed upon you the foundation of blessings, which is creation. So reflect upon it with sound reflection, and be all of you grateful servants. Yet you did not do so despite your capacity; rather, you divided into sects: among you is a disbeliever and among you is a believer.

His saying, ﴿He created the heavens and the earth with truth﴾, means: by an eternal will in accordance with wisdom. Some have said "with truth" means "for the truth," which is the Resurrection.

His saying, ﴿and He formed you and perfected your forms﴾, admits of two interpretations:

First: "Perfected" means He made it firm and sound, in a manner that is not found in this way in anything else. And how could it be found elsewhere, when there exists in their selves powers that indicate, by a particular indication, the oneness of Allah and His lordship, owing to the beauty of this form?

Second: that we direct "beauty" to beauty of appearance. For whoever considers the stature and bearing of the human being and the proportion among his limbs knows that his form is the most beautiful form.

His saying, ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾, means: the Resurrection. He attributed it to Himself because He is the ultimate end of their creation and its purpose. Then He said, ﴿and He formed you and perfected your forms﴾, because it does not necessarily follow from creating a thing that it is shaped in a form, and it does not necessarily follow from having a form that it is among the most beautiful forms. Then He said, ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾, meaning the place of return is to Him alone.

His saying, ﴿He knows what is in the heavens and the earth, and He knows what you conceal and what you disclose, and Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, draws attention by His knowledge of what is in the heavens and the earth, then by His knowledge of what the servants conceal and what they disclose, then by His knowledge of what is in the breasts, both universals and particulars, to show that nothing is hidden from Him, since nothing of the weight of an atom escapes His knowledge at all, in eternity past and future.

In the verse there are discussions:

The first: He is Wise, and it was already foreknown in His knowledge that if He created them they would not do anything except disbelieve and persist in it. So what wisdom prompted Him to create them? We say: When we know that He is Wise, we know that all His acts are in accordance with wisdom, and the creation of this group is His act, so it is in accordance with wisdom. Our lack of knowledge of that does not imply that it is not so; rather, what necessarily follows is that He created them in accordance with wisdom.

The second: He said, ﴿and He formed you and perfected your forms﴾, yet among the individuals of this species there have been those whose form was deformed and whose creation was ugly. We say: there is no ugliness there. Rather, beauty, like other meanings, has levels and ranks. The lowering of some forms below the ranks of what is above them to a clear degree, such that their beauty does not appear, is not outside the bounds of beauty; otherwise, it falls within the domain of beauty and is not excluded from its limit.

The third: His saying, ﴿and to Him is the final return﴾, suggests movement from one side to another, and that is not possible unless Allah were on one side. So how is He? I say: that illusion is with respect to us and our time, not with respect to what is in reality. For reality is far removed from the reality of movement from one side to another, if the one moved toward is exalted above side and direction.

**His saying: (فَآمِنُوا) ("so believe")** may be connected to what came before, because when He, exalted is He, mentioned the punishment that befell the earlier nations for their disbelief in God and their denial of the messengers, He said: "believe" (you) "in God and His Messenger," lest there befall you what befell them of punishment. ﴿And the light which We have sent down﴾, which is the Qur'an, for guidance is sought through it in doubtful matters just as guidance is sought through light in darkness. Al-taghabun (mutual loss and gain) is a reciprocal form (tafa'ul) derived from al-ghabn (deception, loss) in exchange and trade. It is said: ghabanahu yaghbinuhu ghabnan, when one takes something from him for less than its value. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him and his father, said: "Some people are in the Fire being punished, and others are in Paradise enjoying bliss." God, exalted is He, has mentioned concerning the disbelievers that they bought the worldly life in exchange for the Hereafter, and bought misguidance in exchange for guidance. Then He mentioned that their commerce did not profit them, and He directed the believers to a profitable trade, saying: ﴿Shall I direct you to a commerce...﴾ [al-Saff 61:10], to the end of the verse. His saying: ﴿And upon Allah let the believers rely﴾ explains that the believer depends only on Him and is strengthened only by Him, because he believes that the one truly capable is none other than Him.

He said in al-Kashshaf: This is an urging for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to rely upon Him and to be strengthened by Him in his affair, until He gives him victory over whoever denied him and turned away from him. If it is asked: how does ﴿No calamity befalls except by the permission of Allah﴾ connect with what precedes it and relate to it? We say: it relates to His saying: ﴿So believe in Allah and His Messenger,﴾ because whoever believes in Allah and affirms Him knows that no calamity afflicts him except by the permission of Allah.

[Page 25]

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, indeed among your spouses and your children there are enemies to you, so beware of them. But if you pardon, overlook, and forgive, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial, and Allah has with Him a great reward.﴾ ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able, and listen, obey, and spend; it is better for yourselves. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul, those are the successful.﴾

Al-Kalbi said: When a man intended the hijrah (migration), his sons and his wife clung to him and said: "You are going away and leaving us to be lost." So some of them obeyed their families and stayed behind, and Allah warned them against obeying their wives and children. Others did not obey and said: "By Allah, if we do not migrate and Allah does not bring us together with you in the abode of hijrah, we will never benefit you in anything." So when Allah brought them together, He commanded them to spend, to do good, and to show generosity.

Muslim al-Khurasani said: It was revealed concerning Awf ibn Malik al-Ashja'i, whose family and children would discourage him from hijrah and jihad. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, was asked about this verse and said: "These were men from the people of Makkah who had embraced Islam and wanted to come to Madinah, but their wives and children did not leave them alone. This is His saying: ﴿an enemy to you, so beware of them﴾, that is, lest you obey them and abandon hijrah. As for His saying, ﴿But if you pardon and overlook﴾, it refers to the fact that when one of these men migrated and saw that people had preceded him in hijrah and had gained understanding of the religion, he would intend to punish his wife and son who had prevented him from migrating. It means that among your spouses and children there are enemies to you, who forbid you from Islam and discourage you from it, and they are from among the disbelievers, so beware of them. Thus it becomes clear that this enmity is only for disbelief and for forbidding faith, and it does not exist among believers. Believing spouses and children are not enemies to them.

Concerning these spouses and children who prevented them from hijrah, the verse was revealed: ﴿Your wealth and your children are only a trial﴾. Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, said: Do not obey them in disobedience to Allah the Exalted. ﴿A trial﴾ means a test and a distraction from the Hereafter. It was also said: Allah the Exalted informed that wealth and children are a trial for all that befalls people through them, and this is general, encompassing all children. A person is tempted by his child, because he may disobey Allah the Exalted on account of him and commit a forbidden act for his sake, such as seizing the property of another and other things. ﴿And Allah has with Him a great reward﴾, that is, an abundant reward, which is Paradise. He informed that with Him is a great reward so that they would bear the great burden. The meaning is: Do not commit sins on account of your children, and do not prefer them over what is with Allah of great reward.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So fear Allah as much as you are able﴾, Muqatil said: That is, as much as you can. The believer strives in fearing Allah as much as he is able. Qatadah said: This verse abrogated His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾ [Al-Imran: 102]. Some have criticized this and said: It is not sound, because His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Fear Allah with the fear due to Him﴾ does not mean fearing Him in what they are unable to do, since that is beyond their capacity and ability.

As for His saying: ﴿And listen﴾, that is, to Allah, His Messenger, and His Book. It was also said: to what Allah and His Messenger have commanded you. ﴿And obey﴾, that is, Allah in what He commands you. ﴿And spend﴾ of your wealth in the cause of Allah, ﴿it is better for yourselves﴾. The accusative (naṣb) of "better" (khayran) is governed by ﴿spend﴾, as if it were said: "And advance what is better for yourselves." It is like His saying: ﴿Believe, it is better for you﴾ [An-Nisa: 170].

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his own soul﴾. Ash-shuhh is stinginess, and it encompasses wealth and other things. It is said: So-and-so is stingy with wealth, stingy with status, and stingy with kindness. It was also said: "is protected from the injustice of his own soul," so shuhh is injustice. Whoever is far removed from shuhh, that person is among the successful.

If it is asked: "Your wealth and your children are only a trial" indicates that wealth and children are all enemies, and "Indeed among your spouses and your children there are enemies to you" indicates that some of them are enemies and not others. We say: This is within the scope of prevention, for it does not follow that some of the children mentioned earlier, that is, among the children, are those who prevent and those who do not prevent, so that some of them are enemies and not others.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿If you lend to God a good loan, He will multiply it for you and forgive you. God is Appreciative and Forbearing﴾ ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾.

Know that His saying: ﴿If you lend to God a good loan﴾ means: if you spend in the obedience of God, drawing near to Him, He will recompense you with multiplication, because He is (Shakur, "Appreciative") and loves those who draw near to His presence. (Halim, "Forbearing") He does not hasten punishment. (Ghafur, "Forgiving") He forgives you. According to some, the "good loan" is giving charity from lawful wealth. It was said that it is giving charity with a contented heart. The "loan" is that for which a similar return is hoped, namely the reward, like spending in the way of God. In the Kashshaf, he said: mentioning "loan" is a gentle way of soliciting (giving). His saying ﴿He will multiply it for you﴾ means: He will record for you one good deed as ten, and seven hundred, and more increase as He wills. It is read (yud'ifhu), ("He will multiply it").

(Shakur) is a majaz (figurative usage), meaning He does with you what one who greatly appreciates does, namely great reward. Likewise (Halim) means He does with you what one does who forbears toward the wrongdoer, so He does not hasten punishment for you despite the abundance of your sins.

Then someone may say: these actions require knowledge and power, and God mentioned knowledge without power when He said "Knower of the unseen." We say: His saying ﴿the Almighty﴾ indicates power, from "azza" meaning to overcome, and ﴿the All-Wise﴾ indicates wisdom. It was also said: the Almighty is the One whom nothing can frustrate, and the All-Wise is the One to whom error in management never attaches. God is such, so He is Knowing, Powerful, and Wise, exalted is His praise and great is His majesty.

And God knows best what is correct. Praise belongs to God, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon the master of the messengers and the seal of the prophets, our master Muhammad, and his family, and may He grant them abundant peace.
